title: Advisor call: converting Income Fund Class C to Class A
description: Genesys inbound service call from a Miami advisor identified only by phone number. He asks how to convert clients' Contoso Income Fund Class C positions to Class A after the holding period and about the load, fee and tax impact. Harmless rapport (Miami Heat season tickets) should be kept in the note.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Thanks for calling Contoso Woodgrove advisor services, this is Jordan. Who do I have the pleasure of speaking with?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Hi Jordan, it's Carlos Mendez. I have a question about converting share classes for some of my clients.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Hi Carlos, nice to talk to you. Your number matches the advisor we have on file, so we're good on verification. How's your morning going?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Pretty good, thanks. A little tired, though, because I was at the Miami Heat game last night. I'm a season-ticket holder, so my evenings are spoken for.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: That's a great problem to have. So tell me about the share class question.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: I have several clients holding the Contoso Income Fund, Class C. They bought it more than a year ago, so they should be past the holding period, and I'd like to move them into the Contoso Income Fund, Class A.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Understood. Moving from Class C to Class A within the same fund is a share class conversion, and since they're past the holding period there shouldn't be a CDSC on the way out. Is that for all of those clients?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Just the ones in taxable accounts, about a dozen. What does the fee and load impact look like? I don't want to trigger a front-end load on clients who've been with me for years.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: As a general rule, a conversion within the same fund isn't treated as a new purchase, so the front-end load shouldn't apply. You'll want to see the exact fee schedule rather than rely on my memory, though.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That helps. And what about taxes? Are my clients going to see capital gains from the conversion?

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Generally, a conversion between classes of the same fund isn't treated as a sale for tax purposes, so it shouldn't create a gain. Your clients should still confirm that with their tax advisors.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Understood. How does the process work? Is there a form, or can I do it online?

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: There's a class conversion form, and you submit it with a list of the accounts and the share counts. I'll send you the conversion checklist and the form by Wednesday.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Perfect. Could you also send the fee schedule for both classes so I can compare them for my clients?

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Of course. I'll email you the fee schedule tomorrow.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Great. I'll go over the timing with my assistant so the forms are ready when your checklist arrives.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: That works. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: That's all for now. Thanks, Jordan, and go Heat!

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Ha, thanks, Carlos. Enjoy the next game, and thank you for calling Contoso Woodgrove.

gold.notes: Account resolution is by caller phone +1 305 555 0181 only; no email and no firm name is spoken. Keepable rapport: Miami Heat season-ticket holder. The advisor's plan to go over timing with his assistant is a customer commitment and not a task. Due dates: call is Monday 2026-11-16, so 'by Wednesday' is 2026-11-18 and 'tomorrow' is 2026-11-17.
